azureAiChat.connection.markdownDescription:
Connection to your Azure OpenAI resource.

```json
"azureAiChat.connection": {
  "endpoint": "https://my-resource.openai.azure.com",
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "apiKey": ""
}
```

`model` is the **deployment name** from Azure AI Foundry, not the underlying model name. It may also be a list to expose several deployments in the Chat model picker.

Leave `apiKey` empty and run **Azure AI Chat: Set API Key** to keep the key in encrypted SecretStorage instead of this file.

endpoint.markdownDescription: Resource endpoint, e.g. `https://my-resource.openai.azure.com`. No path, no trailing slash.

model.markdownDescription: Deployment name, or a list of deployment names.

apiKey.markdownDescription: Azure OpenAI API key. **Stored as plain text in settings.json** — it syncs with Settings Sync and is committed to git if this lives in a workspace `.vscode` folder. Prefer leaving this empty and using **Azure AI Chat: Set API Key**.

apiMode.markdownDescription: `v1` uses the versionless `/openai/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. Switch to `classic` if you get a 404.

azureAiChat.temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Lower is more deterministic. Ignored by reasoning models that do not support it.

azureAiChat.maxTokens.description: Maximum tokens to generate per response.

azureAiChat.useMaxCompletionTokens.description: Send 'max_completion_tokens' instead of 'max_tokens'. Required by o-series / reasoning-model deployments.

azureAiChat.maxToolIterations.description: Maximum number of tool-calling round trips before the agent loop stops.

enumDescriptions: Fast — explanations, lookups and small snippets. Read-only tools, minimal reasoning.
Thinking — complex changes. Inspects the repository, plans, implements and verifies.
Agent — completes the task end to end, including running checks and fixing failures.
azureAiChat.mode.markdownDescription:
Mode used when the composer's selector is left on **Default**.

`fast` loads only the core prompt and read-only tools, so a "what does this do" question costs a fraction of the tokens. `thinking` adds the investigation and verification guidance. `agent` adds the technology-specific standards and the automatic fix-and-retry loop.

chat.description: The sidebar chat and any single-agent turn. This is the one that runs today.

coordinator.description: Plans the work, aggregates agent results and decides completion. Give this a strong reasoning deployment.

planner.description: Read-only analysis sweeps that run in parallel. A fast, cheap deployment suits this best.

verifier.description: Independently checks the finished work. Give this your strongest deployment — nothing else can approve completion.

azureAiChat.modelRoles.markdownDescription:
Which deployment serves each agent role. Every name here must also appear in `#azureAiChat.connection#` → `model`, which is the list of deployments this extension may call.

```json
"azureAiChat.connection": { "model": ["sol", "luna", "terra"] },
"azureAiChat.modelRoles": {
  "coordinator": "sol",
  "planner": "luna",
  "verifier": "terra"
}
```

Leave a role empty to use the first deployment in the `model` list. A name that is not in that list is reported once and ignored, rather than failing mid-task.

Pointing several roles at one deployment is allowed, but they then share its TPM quota — parallel agents will throttle each other.

enumDescriptions: The direct chat loop this extension has always used.
The same single agent, but run through the Coordinator so task state, file locks and the budget apply.
Full run: parallel planning agents, scoped implementation agents, then an independent verifier with a capped repair loop.
azureAiChat.orchestration.markdownDescription:
How a turn is executed.

`single` is the original loop and the safe default.

`coordinated` routes the same work through the Coordinator — one agent, so the result should be identical, but with the task lifecycle, file locks and the token budget in force.

`multi-agent` runs the full pipeline: five read-only planners in parallel, their plans aggregated into scoped implementation tasks, then an **independent Verification Agent** that re-inspects the repository. A task is reported complete only when verification passes. Expect it to cost several times a single turn — see `#azureAiChat.budget#`.

This setting is the rollback: if a run misbehaves, switch back to `single`.

azureAiChat.maxVerificationAttempts.markdownDescription: How many verify → repair → verify rounds a `multi-agent` run may take before it stops and reports failure. An agent that cannot fix something in three attempts is usually making it worse.

maxTotalTokens.description: Prompt plus completion tokens across a whole run, over every agent.

maxAgents.description: How many agents one run may create in total.

totalTaskTimeoutMs.description: Wall-clock ceiling for a whole run, in milliseconds.

agentTimeoutMs.description: Wall-clock ceiling for a single agent, in milliseconds.

azureAiChat.budget.markdownDescription:
What one run may spend. Reaching a limit stops **new** agents starting; work already in flight is allowed to finish, and the run reports that it was cut short.

Tokens are the limit that matters on a shared deployment: agent mode’s system prompt alone is roughly 12k tokens, so a handful of wide agents costs more than a long run of narrow ones.

maxConcurrentAgents.description: Ceiling across every role at once.

maxPlanningAgents.description: Read-only planning agents running at once.

azureAiChat.concurrency.markdownDescription:
How many agents may run at the same time, globally and per role. Per-role limits apply on top of the global one.

These only take effect once parallel execution lands; with `#azureAiChat.orchestration#` set to `coordinated` today there is one agent per turn.

azureAiChat.autoApproveEdits.description: Apply file edits without waiting for you to review the diff. Off by default.

azureAiChat.includeActiveFile.description: Automatically attach the active editor's file as context with each new message.

azureAiChat.maxFileBytes.description: Files larger than this (in bytes) are truncated when read as context.

azureAiChat.excludeGlobs.description: Globs excluded from file listing and search tools.

azureAiChat.systemPrompt.description: Extra instructions appended to the built-in system prompt. Use this for house style, preferred libraries, or team conventions.

enumDescriptions: Do not send a reasoning effort
Explicitly none — required by some deployments before they accept tools
azureAiChat.reasoningEffort.markdownDescription: Default `reasoning_effort` sent with each request. Only reasoning deployments (o-series, GPT-5 family) accept it — leave empty for everything else. The composer has a per-message override.

azureAiChat.shell.bashPath.markdownDescription: Full path to `bash.exe`. Leave empty to auto-detect Git Bash (Program Files, LocalAppData, or next to `git` on PATH).

azureAiChat.shell.requireApprovalForAll.markdownDescription: Ask before **every** command, including read-only ones like `git status`. Off by default: read-only commands and the project’s own lint/type-check/test/build scripts run immediately, everything that mutates still waits for approval.

azureAiChat.shell.timeoutSeconds.description: Default timeout for a single command. The model may request less, up to a maximum of 600.

azureAiChat.saveSessionHistory.markdownDescription: Write session context (task, decisions, files changed, commands, outstanding items) to the local temp folder so a later session can resume it. Secrets are redacted before writing.

azureAiChat.saveConversations.markdownDescription: Save chat transcripts so they can be reopened and continued from **History**. They are stored on this machine in VS Code's own extension storage folder, not in the temp directory.

languageModelTools.name: azureAiChat_runCommand
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Run a shell command in the workspace using Git Bash on Windows, or the system shell elsewhere. Read-only commands and the project's own lint/type-check/test/build scripts run immediately; anything that changes files, packages, the git repository or the machine asks the user for confirmation first. stdin is closed, so never run anything interactive or any long-running watcher.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Runs shell commands in your workspace, asking before anything that changes state.

command.description: The command line to run, e.g. "git status" or "npm run type-check".

cwd.description: Optional workspace-relative directory. Defaults to the workspace root.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Defaults to 120, maximum 600.

languageModelTools.name: azureAiChat_gitStatus
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show the git working tree status and current branch. Run this before making significant changes so you know what uncommitted work already exists.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads your git working tree status.

languageModelTools.name: azureAiChat_gitDiff
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show the diff of the working tree so you can review exactly what changed. Use it after implementing something, before reporting that you are done.

staged.description: Diff staged changes instead of the working tree.

path.description: Optional workspace-relative path to limit the diff to.

stat_only.description: Return only the summary of files changed.

languageModelTools.name: azureAiChat_runValidation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Discover and run the project's real validation scripts (type-check, lint, test, build) by reading package.json, pyproject.toml or tsconfig.json. Prefer this over guessing command names. Call it after making changes, and report only the outcomes it returns — never claim a check passed that this did not show passing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Runs your project's lint, type-check, test and build scripts.

kinds.description: Which checks to run. Defaults to everything available.

languageModelTools.name: azureAiChat_recordSession
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Record durable technical context for this session — the requirement, a decision and why, a file changed, a bug found or fixed, or a next step. It feeds the session report and lets a later session resume the work. Never record secrets.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Saves notes about this session to the local session report.

kind.description: What sort of entry this is.
